spans.span: While he was doing this, Neville Shandon looked into the room. He had some papers in his hand. Seeing us engaged, he went away again.

spans.anchor: This is Neville Shandon, true enough,” the secretary reported.
spans.span: This is Neville Shandon, true enough," the secretary reported. The identification had taken longer, since the body lay on its face.

spans.anchor: Some darts here. Skene found them at the foot of the hedge.

spans.claim: Ernest Shandon had a nail in his boot and a weak alibi
spans.anchor: I’ve been walking miles with a nail in my boot.
spans.span: I've been walking miles with a nail in my boot." Stenness stepped into the breach once more and explained the state of affairs.

spans.claim: A black silk thread was found in the Maze as a clue
spans.anchor: There’s a bit of black thread lying on the ground.
spans.span: There's a bit of black thread lying on the ground." They stooped over it and examined the fibre.

spans.claim: Ernest Shandon’s cigar-case was found in the Maze
spans.anchor: Wendover’s eye was at once caught by a sparkle from the grass near one of the chairs. He stepped across and picked up a silver cigar-case.
spans.span: They entered the tiny enclosure of Helen's Bower, and Wendover's eye was at once caught by a sparkle from the grass near one of the chairs. He stepped across and picked up a silver cigar-case. Sir Clinton held out his hand for it and glanced at the outside.

spans.claim: Ernest Shandon’s alibi was contradicted by bicycle sightings
spans.anchor: At 4.20 he came upon Ernest squatting by the roadside, about a mile along the public road.

spans.claim: The forged cheque was missing a counterfoil
spans.anchor: The counterfoil of the last missing cheque had been cut out of the book.
spans.span: The counterfoil of the last missing cheque had been cut out of the book. I'd never have noticed it if it hadn't been that I was looking at the numbers.

spans.claim: Ivor Stenness confessed to forging the cheque
spans.anchor: I forged his signature, destroyed the cancelled cheque, cut the counterfoil out of the cheque-book, and cashed the forged cheque.
spans.span: I forged his signature, destroyed the cancelled cheque, cut the counterfoil out of the cheque-book, and cashed the forged cheque. Nobody suspected anything.

spans.claim: Ernest Shandon staged an attack on himself
spans.anchor: He boldly faked up an attack on himself next.
spans.span: So he boldly faked up an attack on himself next. Then, if still another attempt was made, who would suspect the poor victim who had nearly lost his life just a few days earlier?

spans.claim: Ernest Shandon used the Maze and bicycle to commit the murders and escape
spans.anchor: He got to the Maze, went in to his loophole commanding Helen’s Bower.
spans.span: He got to the Maze, went in to his loophole commanding Helen's Bower. There he saw someone whom he took to be Neville Shandon.

spans.claim: Ernest Shandon committed suicide in the Maze
spans.anchor: He’s lying on the ground in Helen’s Bower. I couldn’t see very clearly; but from the way he’s lying, I think he’s done for.
spans.span: He's lying on the ground in Helen's Bower. I couldn't see very clearly; but from the way he's lying, I think he's done for." "Well," said Sir Clinton, "I'd better get into the Maze and make sure of things.

spans.claim: The murderer’s trail stopped at the road after the river bank
spans.anchor: When he reached the road, his trail stopped short.

spans.claim: The air-gun was found hidden in the rhododendrons
spans.anchor: I found it in that clump of rhododendrons out there.
spans.span: I found it in that clump of rhododendrons out there. It had been jammed right into the middle of the bushes; that's why it took so long to find.

spans.claim: Sylvia Hawkhurst was attacked by a poisoned dart during bridge
spans.anchor: Then, as she mechanically brought her hand down again on to the table, Wendover saw a spurt of blood from her right wrist, and, at its source, the brown feathering of one of the poisoned darts embedded in her white skin.
spans.span: Then, as she mechanically brought her hand down again on to the table, Wendover saw a spurt of blood from her right wrist, and, at its source, the brown feathering of one of the poisoned darts embedded in her white skin. For an instant the group around the bridge-table was stricken into immobility, while the blood jetted from Sylvia's wrist and stained the cards across which her hand had fallen.

spans.claim: Ernest Shandon knew the position of the loophole used to kill Roger
spans.anchor: He knew the position of the loophole through which Roger Shandon was shot.
spans.span: And then he let out that he knew the position of the loophole through which Roger Shandon was shot. Speaking of his mythical assailant he said: 'He was at the same loophole as he'd used when he killed Roger.

spans.claim: Sir Clinton used burning sulphur to force Ernest out of the Maze
spans.anchor: He bent his efforts to infusing at least a semblance of harmony into the company, but it was not a very successful attempt.
spans.span: He bent his efforts to infusing at least a semblance of harmony into the company, but it was not a very successful attempt. Sylvia seconded him to the best of her ability; but Arthur still maintained his suspicious attitude; and Ardsley seemed disinclined to emerge from his state of unfriendly neutrality.
